papers.title: Optimization of hybrid gelatin-polysaccharide bioinks exploiting thiol-norbornene chemistry using a reducing additive.
papers.abstract: Thiol-norbornene chemistry offers great potential in the field of hydrogel development, given its step growth crosslinking mechanism. However, limitations exist with regard to deposition-based bioprinting of thiol-containing hydrogels, associated with premature crosslinking of thiolated (bio)polymers resulting from disulfide formation in the presence of oxygen. More specifically, disulfide formation can result in an increase in viscosity thereby impeding the printing process. In the present work, hydrogels constituting norbornene-modified dextran (DexNB) combined with thiolated gelatin (GelSH) are selected as case study to explore the potential of incorporating the reducing agent tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP), to prevent the formation of disulfides. We observed that, in addition to preventing disulfide formation, TCEP also contributed to premature, spontaneous thiol-norbornene crosslinking without the use of UV light as evidenced via1H-NMR spectroscopy. Herein, an optimal concentration of 25 mol% TCEP with respect to the amount of thiols was found, thereby limiting auto-gelation by both minimizing disulfide formation and spontaneous thiol-norbornene reaction. This concentration results in a constant viscosity during at least 24 h, a more homogeneous network being formed as evidenced using atomic force microscopy while retaining bioink biocompatibility as evidenced by a cell viability of human foreskin fibroblasts exceeding 70% according to ISO 10993-6:2016.

summary_zh.motivation: 硫醇-降冰片烯化学的生物墨水存在硫醇基团过早交联导致粘度上升、打印困难的问题。
summary_zh.method: 向明胶-多糖水凝胶中加入还原剂TCEP，通过NMR、AFM等表征探索其浓度对抑制二硫键形成和自发交联的影响。
summary_zh.result: 发现25 mol% TCEP（相对于硫醇量）可在至少24小时内保持粘度恒定，形成更均匀的网络，且保持细胞活力>70%。
summary_zh.validation: 有实验验证：包括流变学、NMR、AFM以及人包皮成纤维细胞活力测试（符合ISO 10993-6:2016）。

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及生物墨水配方优化，但无AI集成，对用户AI驱动生物打印综述的参考价值有限。

papers.title: Fabrication Method for Shape-Controlled 3D Tissue Using High-Porosity Porous Structure
papers.abstract: Shape-controlled 3D tissues resemble natural living tissues in human and animal bodies and are essential materials for developing and improving technologies in regenerative medicine, drug discovery, and biological robotics. In previous studies, shape-controlled 3D tissues were fabricated using scaffold structures or 3D bioprinting techniques. However, controlling the shape of 3D tissues without leaving non-natural materials inside the 3D tissue and efficiently fabricating them remains challenging. In this paper, we propose a novel method for fabricating shape-controlled 3D tissues free of non-natural materials using a flexible high-porosity porous structure (HPPS). The HPPS consisted of a micromesh with pore sizes of 14.87 ± 1.83 μm, lattice widths of 2.24 ± 0.10 μm, thicknesses of 9.96 ± 0.92 μm, porosity of 69.06 ± 3.30%, and an I-shaped microchamber of depth 555.26 ± 11.17 μm. U-87 human glioma cells were cultured in an I-shaped HPPS microchamber for 48 h. After cultivation, the 3D tissue was released within a few seconds while maintaining its I-shape. Specific chemicals, such as proteolytic enzymes, were not used. Moreover, the viability of the released cells composed of shape-controlled 3D tissues free of non-natural materials was above 90%. Therefore, the proposed fabrication method is recommended for shape-controlled 3D tissues free of non-natural materials without applying significant stresses to the cells.

llm.relevance_to_user: 这篇文章涉及生物打印的形状可控组织制造，但完全没有使用人工智能技术。
llm.why_not_core: No AI or machine learning integration; it is a purely fabrication method without data-driven modeling, control, or optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 制造形状可控且无残留非天然材料的3D组织体是一个挑战。
summary_zh.method: 利用高孔隙率多孔结构（HPPS）的微腔室培养细胞，形成形状可控的3D组织。
summary_zh.result: 成功制造I形3D组织，细胞活力高于90%，无需蛋白水解酶。
summary_zh.validation: 通过U-87人胶质瘤细胞培养和释放后的细胞活力验证。

summary_en.motivation: Fabricating shape-controlled 3D tissues without residual non-natural materials remains a challenge in tissue engineering.
summary_en.method: A flexible high-porosity porous structure (HPPS) with a micromesh and I-shaped microchamber was used to culture and shape cells into 3D tissues.
summary_en.result: I-shaped 3D tissues were obtained within seconds of release, with cell viability above 90% and no use of proteolytic enzymes.
summary_en.validation: Cell culture experiments with U-87 human glioma cells and subsequent viability assays confirmed the method's efficacy.
